analysis.title: Cross-Asset Spotlight: Rising Oil, Rising Spreads
key_insights: The 10Y France-Germany spread widened to 174 bps, its highest since 2011. MS Euro Area rates strategists believe the ECB's TPI (Transmission Protection Instrument) would likely only be activated when the spread is above 200bp.
AUD/USD rose 1.3% over the week. MS FX strategists remain bullish on the Australian dollar, citing hawkish central bank commentary that reinforces expectations for tighter policy.
The Hang Seng fell 4.5% over the week. MS China strategists say the correction reinforces their cautious stance, citing renewed foreign outflows, normalised positioning and softer Southbound buying.
Brent rose 6.2% over the week to about $116.72/bbl. MS oil strategists raised their 2027 Brent forecasts because the global refining system faces large refinery maintenance outages between 4Q and 2Q.
MS base-case forecasts for Q2 2027 are S&P 500 7,624 now to 5,900 bear / 8,300 base / 9,400 bull, and Gold 4,013 now to 5,000 base. Base-case Brent is 95 versus 117 currently.

Last week MSCI China (-4.6%) underperformed MSCI ACWI (-0.9%) while the Russell 2000 outperformed (+2.0%). Healthcare (+2.0%) led equity sectors and communication services led losses (-5.4%, a -2.3 SD move).
US and European corporate credit widened broadly at the index level, led by EUR HY (+40bps). The US Treasury curve bull flattened.
BRL gained 1.7% against the USD while MXN fell 0.9%. The EUR TWI fell 0.3%. Brent (+6.2%) outperformed the BCOMSP (-0.5%) while silver (-5.9%) underperformed.
ICI fund flows show US equity outflows of $479bn over 1 week and $499bn over 4 weeks, while taxable bond funds took in $43bn over 4 weeks and $150bn over 13 weeks.

On MS's COVA diversifier scorecard, the top diversifiers are long Consumer Staples vs market (overall score 87), short Copper (86) and short ZARUSD (84). The bottom ones are long Energy vs market (33), long Large vs Small Cap (34) and short Consumer Discretionary vs market (37).
